description:
Programme or Project Overview

Leiden University advertises a PhD candidate position in the research project 'Entangled with Seaweed', working on case studies in Scotland. The project, funded through the Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research (NWO Open Competition), takes an ethnographic approach to the emerging seaweed economy: how coastal communities, industries and regulators in Scotland negotiate the cultivation, harvesting and governance of seaweed, and what this reveals about changing relations between marine resources, livelihoods and environmental policy.

The doctoral candidate will conduct extended ethnographic fieldwork in Scottish coastal communities - interviews, participant observation and document analysis - and contribute to the project's comparative framework alongside the parallel South Africa case. The employment is a salaried four-year PhD position under the Dutch CAO-NU collective agreement with a starting salary of EUR 3,204 per month, based at Leiden's Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology with fieldwork travel to Scotland.

Candidate profile and application

Applicants hold a research master's degree in anthropology, sociology, human geography, marine governance or a related discipline, with strong qualitative research skills and comfort with independent fieldwork. Interest in marine environments, blue economies or environmental anthropology is an advantage. Applications - CV, transcripts, research statement and references - are submitted through the Leiden University careers portal, and the closing date is 7 November 2026.

Highlights

  • PhD on seaweed ethnography - Scotland case studies
  • NWO Open Competition funded project
  • Extended ethnographic fieldwork in coastal communities
  • Salaried four-year position (EUR 3,204 - 4,051 per month)
  • Leiden anthropology and development sociology environment
  • Closing date: 7 November 2026

About Leiden University

Leiden University, founded in 1575, is the oldest university in the Netherlands and a member of the League of European Research Universities (LERU). Its seven faculties in Leiden and The Hague cover humanities, law, social and behavioural sciences, medicine, science, archaeology and governance. Doctoral candidates at Leiden are salaried employees under the CAO-NU collective agreement rather than fee-paying students, which makes its PhD positions fully funded by design. All academic vacancies, including PhD and postdoctoral roles, are advertised on the university's dedicated careers portal.
